newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Supreme Court confirms FPB's insolvency.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Supreme Court confirms FPB's insolvency.

text.p: The Supreme Court confirmed the decision of the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) to place First Private Bank (FPB) under special supervision and seek its insolvency, the BNB said in a statement on Tuesday.
"The Supreme Court rejected on September 30 FPB's appeal against the decision of the BNB to place it under special supervision and dismiss its board of directors," the statement said.

The court's ruling supports BNB's decision in May to open bankruptcy procedures against Bulgaria's biggest private bank, dismiss its management and appoint sequestrators to establish its financial state, said the BNB.
Last month the Sofia City Court postponed its ruling on the FPB's insolvency case for December 11 until the Supreme Court ruled on three appeals filed by the FPB against BNB's decisions.
Hearings on FPB's appeal against BNB's decisison to delete the bank's commercial registration are scheduled for October 25.

The former FPB management has also appealed against the Sofia court's refusal to accept it as a side in the suit because under Bulgarian law, banks placed under special supervision can be represented only by the sequestrators.
The Supreme Court is expected to rule on this third appeal on November 27.

The FPB owes some 31 billion levs to the State Savings Bank and the central bank which were lent to it as refinancing. The bank owes a further 20 billion levs paid out by Post Bank as compensation for individual and company deposits.

The BNB has so far filed insolvency suits against five local commercial banks in line with pledges made to the International Monetary Fund to close debt-ridden banks in a bid to stabilise the shaky banking sector.
A further nine banks were placed under special supervision last week.
